title: General axis-parity matching lemma for finite rectangular boxes
question: For every finite rectangular box with side lengths at least two, does colouring each nearest-neighbour edge by its axis and the parity of its lower endpoint give two matching layers per axis, with the exact rectangular edge-count formula?

finite_contract.box_family: all ordered side triples in [side_min, side_max]^dimension
finite_contract.adjacency: one-coordinate increment by one inside the box

derived_rule.matching_condition: each vertex has at most one incident edge in each layer
derived_rule.parity_separation: the forward and backward candidate lower coordinates differ by one and cannot share parity mod 2

assumptions: Vertices are integer coordinate vectors in a finite rectangular box with every side length at least two.
Edges are only nearest-neighbour coordinate increments and are represented by their unique lower endpoint and axis.
The layer colour is the axis together with the lower endpoint coordinate modulo two; empty colour slots remain part of the layer family.
The Lean incidence lemma is applied to this adjacency relation and does not encode a Q3 operator or physical state.
The side range [2,6] is an exhaustive finite test set for the executable Python rows, while the local incidence proposition is quantified in Lean.
missing_assumptions: A Q3LOCK interaction/operator theorem transferring the combinatorial layers to the full unbounded Hamiltonian.
A representation-independent common core and weighted product-domain estimate for the layer subflows.
Cutoff-, source-, phase-, volume- and exhaustion-uniform boundary commutator and history-tail estimates.
Lie--Trotter/common-alpha convergence, Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification and sector coercivity.
Any physical-empty branch, Reading-H energy comparison, continuum limit or Sector-A completion.
stop_conditions: If a declared box has an invalid side or an edge-count mismatch, fail the sweep.
If any retained layer has two edges incident at one vertex, fail the matching lemma audit.
If the independent reconstruction disagrees with the primary aggregate, retain the disagreement and do not average it away.
Do not promote local matching combinatorics to a Q3 operator, physical, Yang-Mills or mass-gap theorem.
evidence_level: T0 / EXECUTED FINITE ALL-BOX SWEEP WITH A GENERAL LEAN LOCAL-INCIDENCE LEMMA; OPERATOR AND LIMIT INPUTS NOT CLAIMED
non_claims: No Q3LOCK Hamiltonian, Friedrichs-domain or weighted operator theorem.
No boundary commutator, history-tail, common-core, common-alpha or exhaustion theorem.
No OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, broken-sector coercivity, physical-empty comparison, continuum limit or Sector-A/Pre-A closure.
No Yang-Mills dynamics or mass-gap conclusion.

lean_crosscheck.role: Lean proves the abstract local incidence/parity separation and six-colour arithmetic; finite box enumeration and edge counts remain executable Python evidence.

boundary: R-442 closes only the abstract axis-parity matching property and exact edge-count bookkeeping for the declared finite rectangular graph family, with the local incidence statement proved in Lean. It does not close the weighted Q3 split form, operator domains, boundary/history tails, exhaustion, common alpha, KMS/GNS, physical-empty branch, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap claims.
